MAJOR: Reviewer runner now mutates the backlog: `architect_review._ingest` calls `review_ledger.record` → `backlog.update`, contradicting the newly added rule "reviewers… must not edit… backlog… worker/orchestrator persists evidence" and CL-002 (reviewer-only tool).

The documented "one full + one delta re-review" is unachievable at Gate 2: `review_ledger.problems` defaults to `max_reviews=1` in Gate1/Gate2 checks, and `gate2_completion_check` rejects any latest diff evidence with `review_scope=="delta"` (`DELTA_ONLY_REVIEW`), so the delta re-review that is AC-1's whole purpose can never satisfy completion.

`pf_process_check` hard-requires `.github/workflows/pf-gates.yml`, which is declared in `affected_files` but absent from this diff; if it is not present the blocking `pf-process` gate fails and AC-4 ("precheck passes") is not demonstrated.

`architect_review._build_prompt` raises the full-candidate diff cap from 180k to 500k chars, contradicting the "lowest cost/latency" default runner and risking mid-diff truncation/context overflow; no test asserts the bound.
MINOR: `test-framework/tests/conftest.py` autouse fixture forces `PF_BACKLOG_DB=off` for every test, which can silently mask pre-existing DB-mode regressions unless each test explicitly re-enables it.

`design_contract_check._test_exists`/`_evidence_exists` treat any `go test…`/`pytest…` command string and any `://` URL as valid evidence, so coverage can be "satisfied" with nonexistent commands/files.

`framework_ref_check`/`self_review_check` run `git merge-base origin/develop HEAD` with no error handling; a clone/CI without `origin/develop` raises an uncaught RuntimeError from a blocking gate instead of a clean fail-closed message.

The placeholder scan in `design_contract_check` runs over every design_pack string ("tbd/todo/unspecified/not specified/placeholder"), so legitimate prose (e.g., a stop_condition "if a value is unspecified, stop") fails the contract.
`architect_review` diff-mode `design_guardrails` render is wrapped in `except Exception: pass`, silently swallowing failures and contradicting the "no silent failure" invariant/observability goal.

`control_runner` allows arbitrary trailing flags after an allowed prefix (e.g., `go test … -exec <cmd>`), giving the allowlist a command-execution surface; its allowed prefixes also diverge from `guideline-compliance.json` (adds `bash`/`sh`).
`review_ledger._material_ok` compares ISO `at` timestamps as raw strings, so mixed timezone offsets can mis-order `MATERIAL_CHANGE` against the latest review.
`control_gate.current_sha` and `controls()` are duplicated verbatim in `control_runner` (and both re-hash the worktree); no single owner for the candidate-key rule.
NIT: `gate2_completion_check` uses a `for/else` plus a `ledger_bad=[]` sentinel to break out of the per-mode loop; a plain loop with append would not need the sentinel.

`self_review_check.changed_lines` only scans committed `merge-base..HEAD`, so worktree/untracked placeholders bypass it (inconsistent with the encoding gate that explicitly covers worktree/untracked).
`framework_ref_check` bans the literal token `dashboard` in any added line under `core`/`api`/`adapters`/`go`, which will false-positive on legitimate config keys or comments.
SUMMARY: Scope is tooling/docs/config only (no runtime DB/RLS surface, language rule respected), but the review-loop controls are internally contradictory and self-defeating.

Top risk: the new delta re-review path (AC-1) cannot reach Gate 2 — ledger budget=1 plus `DELTA_ONLY_REVIEW` blocks the second diff review, and the reviewer runner writes backlog in violation of its own stated write boundary.
Second risk: blocking gates depend on files/config not present in the candidate (`.github/workflows/pf-gates.yml`, referenced runbooks), so "precheck passes" (AC-4) is unproven.
Recommend reconciling the re-review budget/scope rules with REVIEW-TRIAGE-POLICY, moving backlog persistence out of the reviewer runner, and adding a test for the prompt size cap before Gate 2.
